paper.title: Provably and Practically Efficient Neural Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Neural contextual bandit with smooth activations (NT-kernel RKHS reward)
unmapped: Reward function h lies in the RKHS of the neural tangent kernel of a fully connected net with activations sigma_s(u)=max(0,u)^s; contexts x_{t,a} on the hypersphere S^{d-1}, K per round, chosen arbitrarily
Learner knows the noise sub-Gaussian parameter nu and the NTK RKHS norm S (used in beta)
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic contextual bandit problem, at each discrete sequential step $t=1,2,\dots, T$, for each action $a\in[K]$, a context vector $\bfx_{t}\in \cX$ is revealed... receives the corresponding reward $r_{t} = h(\bfx_{t, a_t})+\xi_t$... (i) The input space is the $d$ dimensional hypersphere... (ii) The reward function $h$ belongs to the RKHS induced by the NT kernel, and $h(\bfx)\in [0, 1]$... (iii) $\xi_t$ are assumed to be conditionally $\nu$-sub-Gaussian

symbols.q_max: maximum batch size max_r q_r used for retraining the neural nets
symbols.gamma_T: maximal information gain Gamma_k(T) of the NT kernel

conditions: Assumption 2: NTK Gram matrix H on all context-action pairs satisfies H >= lambda_0 I
contexts on hypersphere S^{d-1}, h in [0,1] with NTK RKHS norm S
network width m >= poly(T, L, K, 1/lambda, 1/lambda_0, 1/S, log(1/delta))
tuning: fixed batch size q_r for each group
number of training epochs J = Omega_tilde(T), learning rate eta = O(1/T)

source.label: theorem:regret_guarantees
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass1} and \ref{ass2} hold. Consider NeuralGCB given in Algorithm~\ref{alg:NeuralGCB}, with $R$ neural nets, as defined in~\eqref{eq:nn} with $L$ hidden layers each of width $m \geq \text{poly}(T, L, K, \lambda^{-1}, \lambda_0^{-1}, S^{-1}, \log(1/\delta))$. Suppose NeuralGCB is run with a fixed batch size for each group, then the regret~defined in~\eqref{eq:regret_def} satisfies R(T) =\Oct( \sqrt{T \Gamma_k(T)} + \sqrt{T \Gamma_k(T) \log(1/\delta)} +\max_rq_r\Gamma_k(T))

results.notes: Theorem does not explicitly state the probability, but the bound depends on delta and the proof uses high-probability confidence intervals, so recorded as high-probability. Intro states that with Gamma bounds for smooth activations this gives O~(T^{(2d+2s-3)/(2d+4s-4)}), not a formal statement. Appendix also claims O(sqrt(T Gamma log(1/delta)) max_r sqrt(q_r)) for adaptive batch sizes (informal, not recorded).
